clue.text: Top steeplechaser

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a knitted garment worn on the upper body, a sweater
second meaning: a horse that clears fences and water in a race

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the words suggest the best horse in a race, but they are two separate meanings. In Britain a jumper is a sweater.
explanation.definitionFit: A knitted pullover is called this in British English, and a racehorse trained over fences is described the same way.

clue.text: One claiming female is out of shape

indicators.note: to claim something is to take hold of it, so one piece grips another

parts.note: a unit is a single thing, one
F is the standard abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: Someone claims that a woman has let her fitness slip.
explanation.walkthrough: UNIT opens up to take F after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has lost physical condition through lack of exercise is said to be in poor health and lacking stamina.

clue.text: Rising crime clubs across Italy somehow smashed

indicators.note: across means stretching over, so the outer pieces span the rearranged letters
in a down clue rising means read upwards, so the word for crime goes backwards

parts.note: a rap is a criminal charge, as in 'beat the rap'
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

indicators.note: somehow means in some way or other, so the letters of Italy are mixed

explanation.surface: Organised crime groups spreading across Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns RAP into PAR; 'somehow' rearranges ITALY into ALYTI, which PAR and C span.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for extremely drunk, the same as smashed.

clue.text: Firm gets head ousted, no longer in practice

indicators.note: the head is the first letter, and ousting it throws it out of the word

parts.note: trusty means steadfast and reliable, firm

explanation.surface: A company sacks its chief executive and finds itself out of practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' wants to be a company, but it is an adjective meaning steadfast; drop the first letter of TRUSTY.
explanation.definitionFit: A skill that has not been used for some time becomes weakened through neglect, like metal corroding when left idle.

clue.text: Keen to cross area getting extremely rocky

indicators.note: to cross means to go over or span, so the word for keen spreads across the other letters

parts.note: to keen is to wail or cry in grief

indicators.note: extremely means only the outermost letters of getting are used

explanation.surface: Someone eager to traverse a region finds the terrain very rough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' is a verb here, to wail, not an adjective meaning eager.
explanation.definitionFit: Craggy describes ground full of crags, steep rough rocks, so it means rocky.

clue.text: Type of power plant potentially for Iceland, cutting nitrogen

indicators.note: the letters of 'for Iceland' could potentially be rearranged into something else, so they are mixed up
cutting means the nitrogen symbol is cut out of the material before it is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as the anagram material
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: Someone muses about what kind of power station might suit Iceland, minus the nitrogen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting' takes the N for nitrogen out of FORICELAND, leaving FORICELAD, and 'potentially' rearranges those nine letters. Iceland in fact runs on geothermal power, which makes the surface a tease.
explanation.definitionFit: A coal-fired station is one kind of power plant, burning coal to generate electricity.

clue.text: Sharp wake-up call

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a warning that rouses people to danger

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as an abrupt alarm in the morning; the adjective and the noun are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word serves as an adjective for being watchful and quick, and as a noun for a warning signal.

clue.text: Male during May using fancy fitness club

indicators.note: something happening during an event sits inside its span, so one piece goes within the other
fancy means elaborate or ornamented, so the letters are rearranged into something new

parts.note: taken as written
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A man joins an upmarket gym in May, perhaps for the summer.
explanation.walkthrough: M goes into the letters of MAY USING and the whole lot is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A hall or building equipped for physical exercise and training is a place people join to keep in shape.

clue.text: Bishops might be seen with these criminal types

definitions.text: Bishops might be seen with these
definitions.meaning: first meaning: hooked staffs carried by bishops, based on a shepherd's staff
second meaning: dishonest people, thieves and swindlers

explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at bishops keeping bad company; the first half really describes the ceremonial staff a bishop carries.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's hooked crosier is named after the shepherd's staff, and the same word is slang for swindlers and thieves.

clue.text: Remaining peacekeepers considered taking month off

parts.note: the United Nations sends peacekeeping forces

indicators.note: taking something off removes it, so the abbreviation for a calendar period is dropped

parts.note: to muse is to think something over, to consider it

explanation.surface: Peacekeepers who stayed behind thought about taking a month's leave.
explanation.walkthrough: M is the usual abbreviation for month; take it out of MUSED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left over and not yet consumed or employed is still available as surplus stock.

clue.text: Direct judge to release last two Europeans

indicators.note: releasing the final pair lets them go from the end of the word

parts.note: a referee judges a match
E is the abbreviation for European, twice here

explanation.surface: An order to a judge to free the final two European prisoners.
explanation.walkthrough: The last two letters of REFEREE happen to be the two Es, which are dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: To send someone on to another person or place for help or information is to point them there.

clue.text: Experienced politician, say, backing one almost oddly ignored

parts.note: to state something is to say it

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the letters run the other way
ignoring the odd-numbered letters keeps only the even ones

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A seasoned politician, perhaps, supports someone who was almost forgotten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' looks like political support but is the reversal signal. The even letters of 'one almost' are read backwards after STATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior political figure respected for wisdom and long service is the classic description of a respected statesperson.

clue.text: Best theatrical work published previously

indicators.note: previously means earlier, so this piece is placed in front of the other

parts.note: a book that is out has been published
a play is a work for the theatre

explanation.surface: A stage piece hailed as the finest that had already appeared in print.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best' looks like an adjective praising the play, but it is a verb meaning to beat.
explanation.definitionFit: To best an opponent is to defeat them, and doing that in a game means performing better than them.

clue.text: Most act afraid about arresting wealthy individuals

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the letters are read in the other direction
to arrest is to catch and hold, so the words hold the answer within them

parts.note: letters running across the end of the first word, the whole second word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Police mostly shy away from arresting the rich.
explanation.walkthrough: It looks like a charge against timid police, but the answer sits backwards inside the first three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Rich and powerful people, especially overpaid executives, are disparagingly called by this informal phrase.

clue.text: Bribe small number probing smear at intervals

indicators.note: a probe pushes inside something, so these pieces go into the other
taking letters at intervals means every other one, skipping those between

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters
wee is Scottish and informal for small
ten is a number

explanation.surface: A bribe paid to a few people investigating a smear campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small number' looks like a few people, but it is two separate pieces. Wee is everyday Scottish for little.
explanation.definitionFit: A payment or favour offered to win someone over makes a deal more attractive, an informal word for an inducement.

clue.text: Dear sweetheart, formerly deep in thought

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
pensive means lost in thought

explanation.surface: A wistful memory of a former darling, lost in reflection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dear' looks like an endearment to the sweetheart, but it means costly.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage something dear costs a lot of money, so high-priced goods are described this way.

clue.text: Munch, say, orange and win bananas

indicators.note: bananas is slang for crazy, so the letters go wild and rearrange

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone eats an orange and some bananas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Munch' looks like chewing fruit, but it is Edvard Munch, the painter of The Scream; 'say' marks him as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The painter Edvard Munch was born in Norway, so he is an example of a person from that country.

clue.text: Sound having uniform replaced by essentially repairable gear

indicators.note: replaced by means one letter of the sound word is swapped out for new letters

parts.note: a thud is a dull heavy sound
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence or core of the word, its central letters

parts.note: its two central letters are taken

explanation.surface: A noise from a machine whose uniform part has been swapped for gear that can be fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essentially' takes the central two letters of the ten-letter 'repairable', IR, and 'replaced by' swaps them in for the U of THUD.
explanation.definitionFit: Third is one of the forward speeds in a car's gearbox, so it is a gear.

clue.text: Attempts to describe old disastrous events

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw a line around it, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: tries are attempts
aged means old

explanation.surface: Efforts to recount calamities from long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Describe' is used in its geometric sense of drawing a line round a shape, not telling a story.
explanation.definitionFit: Events causing great suffering, destruction or loss of life are commonly called catastrophes or calamities.

clue.text: Subject matter, repeatedly discovered it's not spicy

indicators.note: uncovering a word strips its outer letters, and doing so repeatedly applies it to each word in turn

parts.note: the inner letter once the outer letters and the apostrophe go
the middle letter
the three inner letters

explanation.surface: On the subject of food, it keeps turning out to be bland.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip the first and last letters from each of the last three words and join what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: The theme or issue under discussion in a talk or piece of writing is its subject.

clue.text: Party in hotel, surrounded by rubbish

indicators.note: being surrounded means sitting in the middle with something all round, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: trash is rubbish
H is Hotel in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A party in a hotel leaves the room strewn with litter.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a thrash is a lively party.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses this word for a wild celebration or boisterous social gathering.

clue.text: Beginning to regret no medals sadly for swimmer

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, which alone is kept

parts.note: the opening letter

indicators.note: something gone sadly has gone wrong, so the letters fall out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An Olympic swimmer starts to regret coming home without a medal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' looks like the athlete of the surface, but it means a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: This Pacific fish, also called sockeye, lives in water, so crosswords can call it something that swims.

clue.text: Going topless understood not to upset mathematician

indicators.note: going without a top in a down clue loses the first letter

parts.note: to have understood is to have known

indicators.note: in a down clue upsetting tips a word over so it reads from the bottom up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone saw it coming that going topless would upset a mathematician.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the top is the first letter, and upsetting turns a word upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Isaac Newton co-invented calculus and is one of history's most famous scientists and mathematicians.

clue.text: Children's author needs vast amount of money reportedly

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so it is the spoken form that counts

parts.note: a king's ransom is a huge sum

explanation.surface: A writer for children demands a huge payment.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Ransome wrote Swallows and Amazons, the classic English children's sailing adventure.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Ransome wrote the Swallows and Amazons series of novels for young readers.

clue.text: Immature flier that hurt Grant

parts.note: ow is what people cry when something hurts
to let is to allow, to grant

explanation.surface: A young bird hurt someone called Grant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grant' looks like a person's name thanks to the capital, but it is a verb meaning allow.
explanation.definitionFit: A young bird of prey of the night-hunting kind is called by this diminutive.

clue.text: Force good-for-nothing to return carpentry tool

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for force in physics

indicators.note: returning means going back the way one came, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a waster is an idle good-for-nothing

explanation.surface: A layabout is made to give back a borrowed tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Force' looks like a verb compelling the layabout, but it is just its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: This fine saw with a narrow blade is used by woodworkers for cutting intricate curved patterns.

clue.text: Addict given monetary penalty after promoting drug

indicators.note: to promote is to move up, and in a down clue that shifts a letter higher in the word

parts.note: to be fined is to be given a money penalty
E is short for ecstasy

explanation.surface: An addict fined after pushing drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Promoting' looks like dealing, but it means moving up: the E in FINED climbs one place above the N.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hooked on a habit, such as a dope fiend, is informally described with this word for a devil.

clue.text: Wipe bottom of plate for cream

indicators.note: wiping clears something away, and in a down clue the bottom is the final letter

parts.note: a serving plate

explanation.surface: Clean the base of a dish to use as a cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wipe' suggests cleaning, but it removes the last letter of SALVER.
explanation.definitionFit: An ointment rubbed into the skin to soothe or heal it is a soothing balm or lotion.

clue.text: Floral painting perhaps Dicky breaks is left damaged

indicators.note: breaking into something gets inside it, so one piece goes into the middle of the other
something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
dicky is British slang for unwell or weak

explanation.surface: A painting of flowers is left damaged after something breaks it.
explanation.walkthrough: Dicky is British slang for poorly, as in a dicky heart. ILL goes inside a rearrangement of IS LEFT.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting of arranged flowers is an example of the genre depicting inanimate objects such as fruit and vases.

clue.text: White House facilities outwardly imposing to start with

indicators.note: to start with means at the beginning, so this piece goes in front
the outward part of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters
the facilities is a polite term for the toilet, loo in British English

explanation.surface: The President's residence has grand bathrooms from the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White House' wants to be the Washington residence, but it is a snow house. Loo is British for toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A dome-shaped dwelling built from blocks of snow is literally a house that is white.

clue.text: Some cannot remember flipping London borough!

indicators.note: flipping something turns it over, so the letters read the other way
some means only part of what follows, so the letters are taken from inside a run of words

parts.note: the last three letters of the first word and the first three of the second

explanation.surface: An exasperated person cannot recall the name of a London borough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild British curse, but it signals the reversal. Merton is a borough in south-west London, home to Wimbledon.
explanation.definitionFit: Merton is one of the thirty-two administrative districts making up Greater London.

clue.text: Careers of characters appearing in Morse

definitions.meaning: first meaning: rushes headlong, as a verb
second meaning: the long signals in Morse code, alongside dots

explanation.walkthrough: 'Careers' looks like a noun about jobs, but it is a verb meaning hurtles along. Morse could suggest Inspector Morse, but here it is the code.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to rush along fast, and the long marks of telegraph code share the same word.
